mods.name: Voxel 3D
mods.description: Rebuilds the overworld as a voxel diorama, textured from the cartridge's own tileset and drawn at the window's resolution, and carries the ground past the mesh so the maps around this one stand where the connection graph puts them, with their woods and their towns standing on them and the world past every map standing its own. Past a ring around the camera a tree is the cartridge's own drawing stood up rather than a turned solid, each drawing wearing the one it was cut from, and the distance coarsens in whole pixels. A fight is staged on the map it started on and fills the window with it. Choose it on this page to draw both. The sky takes the hour's own colours out of the cartridge's palette rows, and water draws a waterline where it meets its bank. Doors stand in their walls and the sea past the map's edge is graded like the sea in front of it, and the ANGLE row's LEVEL rung drops the camera low enough to put that sky in the frame. The keys the flat view already zooms with zoom here too, and I and K raise and lower the camera.

mods.name: Randomizer
mods.description: A save-bound run generated from a four-digit seed: Pokemon, wild sources, items, badges, shops, species, moves and trainer teams. Critical placements are accepted only after the host finds no visible self-lock.

mods.name: Follower
mods.description: A Pokemon out of its ball and walking one cell behind you, drawn with the cartridge's own party icon for its species. Pick which slot comes out, whether it stays out on a bike and on the water, and put it away with one press, from the key or from its row in the game's own MODS menu. Face it and press A to pet it: it looks back, cries and wears the cartridge's own heart. It can find hidden items for you too, if you turn that on.

mods.name: Overworld Encounters
mods.description: Replaces random steps with a bounded population of visible roaming wild Pokemon drawn from each map's own encounter tables, with visible shiny Pokemon. Up to sixteen a map, for a screen that shows the whole of one.

mods.name: Hidden Stats
mods.description: A fourth page on a Pokemon's stats screen, in the cartridge's own two-column shape: the four DVs the species was born with, HP's own derived from them, and the stat experience each of the five has trained.

mods.name: Linking Cord
mods.description: The item the later games sell instead of asking for a friend: use it on a Pokemon that only evolves by being traded and it evolves where it stands. Sold on Goldenrod Dept Store's second floor, and spent by the evolution it causes.

mods.name: Quality of Life
mods.description: Seven independent conveniences from later Pokemon games, each off until the player enables it: field moves from owned HMs and badges, automatic Repel renewal, experience from catches, direct PC access, move-effectiveness hints for seen opponents, battle stat-stage summaries and weather indicators.
